text: When a pet needs more of a medication a doctor already prescribed, fill it as a refill. It copies the doctor's directions exactly, and keeps the count of refills right.
Maple is here for a recheck, and her family wants more Carprofen. In Checkout, click Refills.
Every prescription on file is listed, including the ones that came over from eVet. Each shows the refills left, who prescribed it, and the directions.
Apoquel has no refills left. That one needs a new script from the doctor, so it isn't a refill.
Carprofen has two left. Click Use this refill.
Open the line to see it.
It's a refill of that prescription, with who prescribed it and what's left. The directions are locked, so nobody can change them.
Her vaccines from eVet are on her chart too. Click View details.
Here's her rabies dose from eVet, with the vet who gave it.
To reprint the rabies certificate, click Print document,
It's signed by the vet who gave the dose, and shows their license number.
Client liaisons: refills are the one script you can add yourself, because you're only copying directions a vet already wrote.
Two mistakes to avoid: typing new directions instead of using the refill, and changing the vet on a certificate. Use the refill, and let the dose decide the vet.
